name: God's Character
wording: Role: a human summary used to check conclusions after interpreting. It is never a premise, it does not override Scripture, and Scripture may correct it. Agreement proves nothing.

1. Yahweh describes himself as compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in covenant love and faithfulness, and forgiving, yet he does not ignore guilt. This is who he is throughout the story. (Exod 33:18–34:7; Num 14:18; Ps 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2)
2. God is love. His holiness and love belong together: his wrath is never arbitrary but opposes what destroys what he loves, and his compassion holds back his anger. (1 John 4:8, 16; Hos 11:8–9)
3. He comforts like a mother and protects fiercely. (Isa 49:15; 66:13; Matt 23:37)
4. Mercy and justice meet at the cross: God himself bears the cost of guilt, so forgiveness is real and justice is upheld. (Rom 3:25–26; 5:8)

5. Jesus reveals this character: full of grace and truth, eating with sinners, healing the unclean, forgiving the guilty and standing for the oppressed; whoever has seen him has seen the Father. (John 1:14, 18; 14:9; Heb 1:3)

Check: does a reading make God arbitrary, cruel for its own sake, indifferent to evil, unfaithful to his promises, or unlike Jesus? Then examine both the reading and this summary again against Scripture.
